issues.source_quote: А она меня яростно обвивалась то Бульварным кольцом, то Садовым кольцом.
issues.translation_quote: And it fiercely wound itself around me, now with the Boulevard Ring, now with the Garden Ring.
issues.justification: The subject/object relationship is reversed. Moscow is wrapping itself around him, not 'it wound itself around me' in a neutral spatial sense. The Russian anthropomorphizes the city embracing/entangling him; the English is awkward and blunts the image.

issues.source_quote: ...пока окончательно оглушенного не отпускала для передышки в коммунальный очаг у Покровских ворот.
issues.translation_quote: ...until, completely stunned, it finally let me catch my breath at a communal hearth by the Pokrovsky Gate.
issues.justification: 'communal hearth' is overly literal and unnatural in dialogue/narration here. It weakens the nostalgic Soviet-era domestic image of a communal flat.

issues.source_quote: Маргарита Павловна Хоботова, женщина весомых достоинств
issues.translation_quote: Margarita Pavlovna Khobotova, a woman of substantial merits
issues.justification: This misses the comic nuance of 'весомых достоинств', which hints both at literal physical heft and figurative importance. 'substantial merits' sounds stiff and loses the humor of the narrator's phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: dismissed yet still fully admitted
issues.justification: The phrasing is unnatural in English and sounds bureaucratic rather than witty. The Russian is a compact ironic characterization of the ex-husband's odd status in the household.

issues.source_quote: Ан удивительный тройственный союз, возбуждавший мой живой интерес.
issues.translation_quote: An amazing three-way union, which greatly piqued my interest.
issues.justification: 'three-way union' carries unintended sexual overtones in English and disrupts tone/period feel. The Russian is amused and ironic, not suggestive in that way.

issues.source_quote: Что значит не хочется, Лева? С утра заправляйся. Мозги, они тоже этого требуют.
issues.translation_quote: What do you mean, not hungry, Lyova? Fuel up in the morning. Your brains need it too.
issues.justification: 'Не хочется' means 'don't feel like it,' not necessarily 'not hungry.' The shift subtly changes the exchange and flattens the maternal/scolding tone.

issues.translation_quote: That cheerful fellow
issues.justification: 'cheerful fellow' is serviceable but weak; the Russian colloquial-nostalgic 'веселый малый' has more period flavor and characterful warmth than this bland phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: a performer of couplets and feuilletons
issues.justification: 'feuilletons' is not idiomatic for English subtitles and will mean little to many viewers. It preserves the Russian word instead of conveying the Soviet variety-performer genre and comic self-presentation.

issues.source_quote: говорит, что за мир он стеной
issues.translation_quote: he says he stands for peace like a wall
issues.justification: This is awkward literalism. The slogan-like idiom needs a more natural equivalent such as 'he says he's solidly for peace' to sound performable.

issues.source_quote: И для них я исполню еще одно произведение... моего друга, не побоюсь этого слова, популярнейшего поэта Соева.
issues.translation_quote: And for them I will perform one more work... by my friend, not to be afraid of the word, the most popular poet Soyev.
issues.justification: 'not to be afraid of the word' is a literal calque that fails as spoken English and kills the comic emcee flourish. A joke/style beat fails to cross into English, which is a major artistic loss.

issues.source_quote: Что это? Прости, я воспользовался твоим бразильским феном.
issues.translation_quote: Khobotov, what’s that? Sorry, I used your Brazilian hairdryer.
issues.justification: 'Бразильский фен' is almost certainly a joking reference to a Brazilian phonograph record/recording or some other comic domestic item, not literally a 'Brazilian hairdryer.' The literal rendering is confusing and likely wrong in context.

issues.translation_quote: We made it. That’s how we do it. That’s the way.
issues.justification: These youth-slang lines are flattened into generic modern English. The Russian has a very specific colloquial swagger; the translation loses character voice and period slang texture.

issues.source_quote: А ты тут и вертишься своевременно.
issues.translation_quote: And you show up right on time.
issues.justification: 'вертишься' suggests hovering around/helpfully bustling about, with ironic innuendo about Savva's convenient presence. 'Show up right on time' narrows the meaning and loses the comic implication.

issues.source_quote: Ну и ловок же ты сверхъестественно.
issues.translation_quote: Man, you’re supernaturally nimble.
issues.justification: The line is supposed to sound teasing and colloquial; this comes out bizarre and unnatural in English, missing the bantering tone.

issues.source_quote: Да уж Савва, семью ты разбил. Крепкую советскую семью. В прах разметал домашний очаг.
issues.translation_quote: Well, Savva, you broke up a family. A solid Soviet family. Scattered the home hearth to dust.
issues.justification: The mock-dramatic Soviet cliché is important to the humor. 'Scattered the home hearth to dust' is clumsy and non-idiomatic, so the parody of solemn moralizing doesn't land.

issues.translation_quote: Me, of course, stood at attention.
issues.justification: As rendered, this sounds merely literal. In Russian it's a comic military self-characterization in colloquial speech; the English needs more idiomatic humorous force.

issues.translation_quote: studies South America
issues.justification: This is understandable, but in context it suggests scholarly specialization; 'works on South America' or 'specializes in South America' would fit better.

issues.translation_quote: You gave injections wonderfully.
issues.justification: This sounds unintentionally comic and unidiomatic. The Russian is gently awkward/flirtatious, but natural within context; the English should preserve that without sounding absurd.

issues.translation_quote: she has an intense spiritual life
issues.justification: The phrase is ironic and socially specific; in English 'spiritual life' reads overly religious or earnest. The intended dry humor about an overintellectual wife is weakened.

The counting gag continues through the scene and depends on brisk comic rhythm. The translation is literal but misses opportunities to make the joke sound natural and performable in English subtitles.

issues.translation_quote: Let me kiss your hand.
issues.justification: In English this is acceptable, but the register here should preserve the overly formal gallantry that marks Khobotov's character. The current phrasing is flatter and less courtly than the Russian construction.

issues.translation_quote: vitamin shots are popular
issues.justification: The Soviet-era clinical jargon and understated joke are reduced to plain explanatory language. The translation loses period texture and Khobotov's evasive modesty.

issues.source_quote: Большая проблема, темперамент, но одновременно экономия средств.
issues.translation_quote: A big problem, temperament, but at the same time economizing on means.
issues.justification: This is awkward and opaque in English. The Russian is pseudo-critical talk about artistic craft; the English reads as broken literalism.

issues.source_quote: Он сомнителен... Я бы ему не доверял.
issues.translation_quote: He’s dubious... I wouldn’t trust him.
issues.justification: This misses the comic pomposity of Velyurov's suspicion. 'He's somewhat questionable' or similarly stylized phrasing would better preserve voice; 'dubious' sounds off for a person.

issues.translation_quote: Selling your body?
issues.justification: Comprehensible, but bluntly modern/idiomatic in a way that jars with the scene. The Russian line is teasing and slightly risque, not quite this contemporary in feel.

issues.translation_quote: some silly little nobody from an alley
issues.justification: The Russian rhyme and comic colloquialism are central to Sveta's voice. The English is semantically close but loses the catchy, dismissive zing.

issues.source_quote: Ты не забудь, сегодня придут Орловичи.
issues.translation_quote: Don’t forget, the Orloviches are coming today.
issues.justification: The surname is mishandled as an English plural form. In Russian this is a family name; in subtitles it should be rendered naturally, e.g. 'the Orloviches' only if consistently anglicized, but elsewhere nuances around singular/plural family reference become confusing.

issues.translation_quote: If it ends early, I’ll wait.
issues.justification: The flirtatious simplicity of the Russian turns stiff here. The line sounds computational rather than like natural spoken English.

issues.translation_quote: And who doesn't drink? Pray, tell me, name them!!
issues.justification: The famous comic line is overtranslated into melodramatic English. The Russian is sharp, colloquial, aphoristic; this version sounds theatrical in the wrong way.

issues.translation_quote: master of the artistic word
issues.justification: Calque. This Soviet honorific/performance formula needs idiomatic rendering or adaptation; untranslated literally, it sounds bizarre and loses cultural force.

issues.translation_quote: And you’ve gone and misplaced your referral somewhere.
issues.justification: The speaker is talking about his own referral in self-mocking continuation, not accusingly pointing at 'you.' Wrong pronoun changes the line's meaning and interpersonal tone.

issues.translation_quote: one must give up seats to the elderly
issues.justification: The joke is that he gallantly offers his seat and she teasingly frames him as elderly. The English is too generic and misses the lightly comic sting.

issues.translation_quote: What an evolved... highly e-v-volved relationship!
issues.justification: 'Высокие отношения' means 'lofty/high-minded relations,' not 'evolved.' The mistranslation distorts a key recurrent ironic refrain and loses its comic-social resonance.

issues.source_quote: Это Камойнс? Нет, это Франсуа Вийон.
issues.translation_quote: Is that Camoens? No, that’s François Villon.
issues.justification: Across the sequence of poet references, the translation is often semantically adequate, but the deadpan running joke depends on nimble rhythm. Here and elsewhere the English is serviceable yet too stiff, weakening a major comic pattern.

issues.translation_quote: he loves him very much
issues.justification: In context this is dry irony from Margarita Pavlovna about Savva and Khobotov, but the literal English may be read straightforwardly. A more strategic rendering is needed to preserve the social comedy.

issues.translation_quote: Our folks are playing at French life.
issues.justification: This sounds unnatural and misses the sardonic flavor. The line comments on pretentious pseudo-French behavior; the English should be more idiomatic.

issues.translation_quote: Mon papa, ne je pas, que je danse, que je danse!
issues.justification: The faux-French refrain is reproduced mechanically but not shaped for comic comprehensibility. Since the Russian itself plays with garbled French, the English needs framing or adaptation to preserve the joke rather than merely reproducing nonsense.

issues.translation_quote: for kindergarten you’re... too bulky
issues.justification: This is literal to the point of clumsiness. Margarita's insult should be sharp and witty; 'too bulky for nursery school' does not sound like natural English repartee.

issues.translation_quote: secret erotomaniacs
issues.justification: A literal cognate that sounds clinical and odd in English, flattening the comic insult. The phrase should feel barbed and characterful, not translated jargon.

issues.translation_quote: That’s a healthy view of the matter.
issues.justification: Not outright wrong, but in context 'здоровый' has a colloquial approving sense like 'sound' or 'sensible.' The literal 'healthy' is infelicitous and weakens the lively workshop banter.

issues.translation_quote: You were splendid.
issues.justification: The idiom means more like 'you rose to the occasion' or 'you were at your best.' 'splendid' sounds generic and misses the ironic solemnity of the toast-like praise.

issues.translation_quote: Inu zête ridicule, mon ami.
issues.justification: The faux-French phrase is malformed in a way that becomes meaningless in English letters. Since the joke is performative code-switching, the subtitling should either normalize or signal the intended phrase instead of producing unreadable gibberish.

issues.source_quote: Ты течешь, как река. Странное название.
issues.translation_quote: You flow like a river. A strange name.
issues.justification: This line comments on the song title and is semantically carried over, but 'name' is wrong: it refers to the title of the song. This is a concrete mistranslation.

issues.translation_quote: Your pedestrians are small people.
issues.justification: 'люди невеликие' here means ordinary/unassuming people, not literally 'small people.' The literal rendering sounds demeaning and misses Okudzhava's affectionate tone.

issues.source_quote: Никогда до конца не пройти тебя.
issues.translation_quote: You can never walk you through to the end.
issues.justification: This is ungrammatical and seriously disrupts the lyric. A clear fluency failure.

issues.translation_quote: The dear aquarium is asleep.
issues.justification: The phrase is poetically odd in Russian too, but 'dear aquarium' sounds awkwardly literal and may puzzle unnecessarily in English.

issues.translation_quote: A stage man must be a provocateur
issues.justification: 'задира' is more like a scrapper/teaser/troublemaker, not 'provocateur.' The choice sounds too ideological/modern and shifts Velyurov's self-description.

issues.translation_quote: Phalaecian hendecasyllable
issues.justification: Terminologically fine, but the surrounding passage reads like a raw transcription rather than spoken recitation; the academic rhythm is not well naturalized for subtitles.

issues.translation_quote: A troubadour from Languedoc.
issues.justification: 'трувер' is technically 'trouvère,' not 'troubadour.' The distinction may be minor for general audiences, but the film characterizes Khobotov via such learned references.

issues.translation_quote: You’re all достоинства.
issues.justification: The Russian word is left untranslated, producing overt untranslated material and a broken line.

issues.translation_quote: And this кружение...
issues.justification: Untranslated Russian remains in the subtitle, breaking immersion and meaning.

issues.translation_quote: as a person, he’s very good
issues.justification: This is stilted and unnatural. In context it should sound colloquial and lightly ironic, not like ESL phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: A master of the artistic word—that’s a writer.
issues.justification: The joke about inflated self-description depends on idiomatic English. Because the phrase itself was calqued earlier, the payoff here also fails.

issues.translation_quote: Margarita Pavlovna said not to задерживаться.
issues.justification: Untranslated Russian remains in the English subtitle.

issues.translation_quote: the будущий husband
issues.justification: Partially untranslated phrase. This is a clear subtitle error.

issues.translation_quote: неизменно. Sentries are supposed to смена
issues.justification: The song contains multiple untranslated Russian words and broken syntax, seriously damaging poetic sense and subtitle usability.

issues.source_quote: Он светел, бодр и молод душой.
issues.translation_quote: He’s bright, бодр, and young at heart.
issues.justification: Untranslated Russian adjective left in place.

issues.translation_quote: help a фронтовой friend.
issues.justification: Untranslated Russian remains in a normal dialogue line.

issues.translation_quote: You’re the mouthpiece of the эпоха!
issues.justification: Untranslated Russian noun left in place.

issues.source_quote: Мой отец запрещал, чтоб я польку танцевала / танцевал.
issues.translation_quote: My father forbade me to dance the polka
issues.justification: This loses the joke's key gender switch and symmetrical structure unless the masculine/feminine versions are clearly distinguished. The humor of the reveal is weakened.

issues.translation_quote: Like a школьник.
issues.justification: Another untranslated Russian word, and also a missed voice choice. The line should sound emotionally exposed and colloquial in English.

issues.translation_quote: your aunt has completed your corruption.
issues.justification: 'completed your corruption' is too literal and stilted. The Russian has witty mock-moral indignation; the English lands awkwardly and misses the social-comic tone.

issues.translation_quote: lets her пережить the play of passions
issues.justification: A Russian word is left untranslated inside the English subtitle. This is a clear untranslated-material error and breaks comprehension.

issues.translation_quote: You... You’re отказваетесь of me?
issues.justification: The key verb is left in Russian and even misspelled/transliterated inconsistently, making the line incomprehensible in English at an emotionally crucial moment.

issues.source_quote: Не знать ни падений, ни взлетов.
issues.translation_quote: To know neither падения nor взлеты.
issues.justification: Two central nouns are left untranslated. This is a serious accuracy failure in an important rhetorical speech.

issues.translation_quote: Don’t мельтешись.
issues.justification: The imperative is left untranslated, producing non-English output and losing the colloquial meaning ('don't fuss/flit about').

issues.translation_quote: a смена of underwear
issues.justification: The noun is left untranslated in a practical instruction. This is a straightforward untranslated-material error.

issues.source_quote: Не ем, не пью, тревожусь в час ночной.
issues.translation_quote: I neither eat nor drink, I тревожусь at night.
issues.justification: The verb remains in Russian, so the poetic line is incomplete and not understandable to an English viewer.

issues.translation_quote: you might слегка adjust your last name
issues.justification: The adverb is left in Russian, interrupting comprehension and tone in a comic exchange.

issues.translation_quote: More звучно
issues.justification: The adjective/adverb is left untranslated, creating broken English and losing the intended comic suggestion about the surname sounding more sonorous.

issues.translation_quote: and I looked for you at the кино
issues.justification: The key noun is left untranslated. In a song lyric this especially breaks flow and singability.

issues.translation_quote: I was in a санаторий.
issues.justification: The place noun is left in Russian rather than translated or adapted ('sanatorium'/'rest home'), leaving non-English material in the subtitle.

issues.source_quote: Тетя - дивное существо. Но ей не хватало в жизни событий.
issues.translation_quote: Auntie is a marvelous creature. But she lacked events in her life.
issues.justification: 'Lacked events in her life' is overly literal and unnatural in English dialogue. It misses the idiomatic sense that her life lacked excitement/incidents.

issues.source_quote: Одиночество и беллетристика. Вот что осталось в удел этой женщине.
issues.translation_quote: Loneliness and fiction. That’s what fell to this woman’s lot.
issues.justification: 'Fiction' flattens the slightly old-fashioned 'беллетристика', and the whole line sounds stiffly literal rather than witty, theatrical spoken English. The character voice loses elegance and period flavor.

issues.translation_quote: like Soyev’s pince-nez
issues.justification: The joke depends on knowing the ridiculousness of Soyev's pince-nez within the film's world; without any adaptation, the comparison is opaque and the humor largely fails to land for an English viewer.

issues.source_quote: И только вы проявили себя как безусловный враг человечества.
issues.translation_quote: And only you showed yourself as an outright enemy of humanity.
issues.justification: 'Showed yourself as' is awkwardly literal. The line should sound like sharp conversational invective; here it reads translated rather than spoken.

issues.source_quote: На досуге обдумайте свое поведение и дайте телеграмму Свете. Вас ждут.
issues.translation_quote: In your spare time, think over your behavior and send Sveta a telegram. She’s waiting.
issues.justification: 'In your spare time' is the wrong idiom and weakens the dry comic sting of 'На досуге'. 'She's waiting' also misses the impersonal 'you are expected'.

issues.translation_quote: She’s waiting.
issues.justification: The Russian means 'you are expected/they're waiting for you,' not specifically 'she's waiting.' The singular subject narrows the meaning incorrectly.

issues.translation_quote: Play, Yashen’ka, play!
issues.justification: Leaving the diminutive name in transliteration without adaptation is not itself wrong, but the line misses the sports-commentary exuberance and colloquial warmth. It sounds wooden rather than like a lively shouted cheer.

issues.source_quote: Будешь у нас на глазах. Так спокойней.
issues.translation_quote: You’ll be under our eyes. It’s calmer that way.
issues.justification: Both phrases are literal calques. Natural English would be 'We'll be able to keep an eye on you. It's more reassuring that way.' As written, the controlling tone lands awkwardly and non-idiomatically.

issues.translation_quote: a burden that is utterly impossible
issues.justification: This is unidiomatic and semantically off. A burden is not 'impossible'; it is 'too much to bear', 'unbearable', or 'more than she can carry'.

issues.source_quote: И где вам навсегда предстоит вернуться в ледниковый период. Но только без шкур
issues.translation_quote: And where you will have to return forever to the Ice Age. But without furs
issues.justification: The phrasing is stilted and unnatural in English comedy. It loses the rhythm and comic bite of Margarita's tirade.

issues.translation_quote: read you poems, wrapped you in quotes
issues.justification: 'Wrapped you in quotes' is a literal rendering that misses the ironic, seductive image of 'enveloping/smothering you in quotations.' The humor and characterization suffer.

issues.source_quote: А вы еще встретите человека и поскладнее и посвежее.
issues.translation_quote: And you’ll still meet a man more solid and fresher.
issues.justification: 'More solid and fresher' is not natural English and does not capture Margarita's patronizing, appraising tone. The cutting humor is blunted.

issues.translation_quote: The impious murderer plunged a dagger into Delarue’s chest. The latter, taking off his hat, said politely: thank you!
issues.justification: This epigram should land as absurdly polished comic verse. 'The latter' is scholastic and deadens the wit; the line reads like a crib translation rather than a pointed literary quotation.

issues.translation_quote: lived by your mind
issues.justification: This is an unnatural calque. The meaning is 'lived by your judgment/under your guidance' or 'used your brains instead of my own.'

issues.source_quote: И каждый проворный кляузник вешал бы на тебя собак.
issues.translation_quote: And every nimble informer would have hung dogs on you.
issues.justification: The idiom 'вешать собак' is translated literally and becomes nonsensical in English. It should be something like 'would have pinned everything on you/slung every accusation at you'.

issues.source_quote: Жить в пол ноги, работать в пол силы.
issues.translation_quote: To live half a life, work half-strength.
issues.justification: The phrase is rhetorically vivid in Russian; the English feels like a literal note. It needs a more idiomatic, forceful rendering to preserve the emotional crescendo.

issues.translation_quote: The only progressive view.
issues.justification: The Russian means 'the only truly progressive point of view' or, idiomatically, 'the only sensible modern view.' 'The only progressive view' sounds odd and underspecified in context.

issues.translation_quote: When you step out on stage, You must strive for one thing: To tell everyone at once Who you are, what for, and why.
issues.justification: The comic recitation sounds translated rather than performable English verse. 'what for' is especially awkward and fails to reproduce the satirical patter.

issues.source_quote: Все стало вокруг голубым и зеленым.
issues.translation_quote: Everything around turned blue and green.
issues.justification: This famous lyric sounds clumsy in English; 'turned blue and green' evokes color change rather than springtime freshness. The song's lyrical effect is weakened.

issues.translation_quote: Your pajamas are hanging on you.
issues.justification: Unidiomatic. In English one would say 'Those pajamas are hanging off you' or 'They’re swallowing you up.'

issues.source_quote: Боже мой, сколько в вас чистоты.
issues.translation_quote: My God, how much purity there is in you.
issues.justification: This is grammatically understandable but deeply unnatural and fails as intimate dialogue. It should evoke emotional admiration, not abstract moral vocabulary.

issues.source_quote: К нам в 19 кабинет приходила одна дама
issues.translation_quote: A lady came to our office 19
issues.justification: 'Cabinet' in Russian medical usage is 'consulting room/room', not 'office 19'. The chosen term sounds wrong for a hospital setting.

issues.translation_quote: Imagine, I’m afraid to say a word.
issues.justification: The line is repeated as a comic mannerism, but this rendering is too literal and colorless. It misses the flirtatious, slightly old-fashioned tone.

issues.source_quote: Очень жаль, что вы не грассируете.
issues.translation_quote: Too bad you don’t roll your R’s.
issues.justification: 'Грассировать' refers specifically to a French-like uvular r, a comic marker of affected charm. 'Roll your R's' points to the opposite articulation and misses the joke.

issues.source_quote: В больнице я не лежал. Я был в санатории. Тоже не сахар.
issues.translation_quote: I wasn’t in the hospital. I was in a санаторий. Not sugar either.
issues.justification: 'Not sugar either' is a literal idiom that fails completely in English. The sardonic tone should be rendered as 'No picnic either' or similar.

issues.source_quote: Ну, Лев Евгеньевич, пора делать выбор. Боритесь за права мужчины и человека!
issues.translation_quote: Well, Lev Yevgenyevich, time to make a choice. Fight for the rights of man and human being!
issues.justification: 'man and human being' is a literal and awkward rendering that ruins the comic sloganizing. The line should sound punchy and theatrically absurd.

issues.source_quote: Какой, понимаешь, это простор. Такая воля. Гуляй - не хочу.
issues.translation_quote: Such space, you know. Such freedom. Roam as you please.
issues.justification: The colloquial, delighted idiom is flattened into awkward literal phrasing. It fails to sound like lively spoken English.

issues.source_quote: Живут не для радости, а для совести.
issues.translation_quote: You don't live to be happy, you live to do your duty.
issues.justification: This substitutes a moral commonplace for the specifically Russian contrast between joy and conscience. The aphoristic flavor and cultural resonance are significantly altered.

issues.translation_quote: The game goes into the endgame
issues.justification: The chess metaphor is understandable but awkwardly literal; in English one would say 'We've reached the endgame.' The current phrasing weakens Kostik's playful theatricality.

issues.source_quote: Если они меня увезут туда, мне уже больше не будет исхода.
issues.translation_quote: If they take me there, there will be no way out for me anymore.
issues.justification: This is grammatical but wooden and melodramatically flat. The Russian has a desperate, memorable cadence that is not recreated.

issues.translation_quote: A player or a bath attendant?
issues.justification: 'Лицедей' is not 'player'; it means actor/mime/performer, with a theatrical, slightly elevated flavor. The contrast joke with 'bath attendant' is damaged.

issues.source_quote: Ни пуха, ни пера. - К черту.
issues.translation_quote: break a leg. To hell with it.
issues.justification: The set exchange is mistrendered in its response. After 'break a leg,' the standard equivalent would be 'Thanks' or another adapted ritual; 'To hell with it' misses the formulaic theatrical joke.

issues.source_quote: Ну, знаете, если вам не нравится мой выходной костюм!
issues.translation_quote: Well, if you don’t like my weekend suit!
issues.justification: 'Weekend suit' is not idiomatic here and loses the comic self-importance of 'dress/best suit'.

issues.translation_quote: Under the mask of a sheep there lurked a lion.
issues.justification: This is understandable but stiff and literary in the wrong way. The joke calls for a more nimble mock-high style; 'mask of a sheep' is especially awkward.

issues.source_quote: О, если бы моя тугая плоть могла растаять
issues.translation_quote: Oh, if only this solid flesh of mine could melt
issues.justification: This mangles the Shakespeare echo. The high-cultural joke depends on recognizability; 'solid flesh' is the established phrase, not 'this solid flesh of mine,' and the surrounding setup is clumsy.

issues.source_quote: Не далее как сегодня я уже выслушал подобный упрек.
issues.translation_quote: Just today I already heard such a reproach.
issues.justification: The arch, mock-formal tone is flattened. 'Listened to such a reproach' is not idiomatic English and weakens Kostik's cultivated voice.

issues.translation_quote: The 60s had died down. The 70s flew by. The 80s sprouted.
issues.justification: 'The 80s sprouted' is a literal calque that sounds bizarre in English. The sequence should preserve the poetic personification without becoming absurdly awkward.

issues.translation_quote: Auntie
issues.justification: 'Auntie' can sound childish or overly cutesy in English. Depending on context, 'my aunt' might better fit the adult ironic tone.

issues.source_quote: В непосредственной близости от Покровских ворот.
issues.translation_quote: in immediate proximity to Pokrovsky Gate.
issues.justification: Overly bureaucratic phrasing. Something like 'right by Pokrovsky Gate' would sound more natural in dialogue.

issues.translation_quote: Oh, come on!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but it slightly softens the indignant conversational energy of the Russian.

issues.translation_quote: the solemn day of the marriage registration
issues.justification: 'Marriage registration' is technically understandable but bureaucratic and unromantic; it jars with the mock-grand style of the line.

issues.source_quote: Мой друг Совранский чуть не врезался в самосвал
issues.translation_quote: my friend Sovransky nearly crashed into a dump truck
issues.justification: Grammatically fine, but 'crashed into a dump truck' sounds more like an accident report than a lively anecdote.

issues.source_quote: Сделаю все, что в моих силах.
issues.translation_quote: I’ll do all I can.
issues.justification: Natural enough, but slightly flat versus the more formal politeness of the Russian.

issues.translation_quote: Yes... The situation is becoming dangerous.
issues.justification: This sounds literal and abstract. Something like 'This is getting dangerous' would fit spoken English better.

issues.translation_quote: Yes, the stands are full today.
issues.justification: Comprehensible, though 'packed' would sound more idiomatic and energetic for sports commentary.

issues.translation_quote: Fine. Wonderful.
issues.justification: The progression is slightly odd in English; the Russian cadence is concise and conversational.

issues.translation_quote: I’d better go.
issues.justification: This is acceptable, but 'I think I should leave' might better capture the embarrassed withdrawal in context.

issues.translation_quote: He’s a vividly colored person
issues.justification: Understood, but unusual collocation in English. A more idiomatic phrase would preserve the comic evaluation better.

issues.translation_quote: I love her!
issues.justification: Accurate, but the repeated rhythm and hysteria might need punctuation/variation for stronger dramatic effect in subtitles.

issues.translation_quote: Stabbing pain.
issues.justification: As a clipped answer to a question, this is somewhat unnatural. 'A stabbing pain' or 'Sharp pain' would read more smoothly.

issues.translation_quote: medical worker
issues.justification: Accurate, but slightly bureaucratic in English. 'I work in medicine' would sound more natural in dialogue.

issues.translation_quote: Imagine—
issues.justification: Not wrong, but repeated use in English can feel stilted; context might favor 'Would you believe it' or similar colloquial phrasing.

issues.translation_quote: You look triumphant.
issues.justification: Natural, but somewhat plain; the Russian has a slightly more pointed, witty flavor.

issues.translation_quote: Who are you teaching?
issues.justification: Literal. A more idiomatic English retort would be 'Who are you lecturing?' or 'Who are you telling?'

issues.translation_quote: steel friend
issues.justification: Literal but not transparent in English; the comic epithet for a vehicle would benefit from adaptation.

issues.translation_quote: My respects.
issues.justification: Understandable but archaic in an awkward way. 'My respects to you' or a more natural greeting would work better.

issues.translation_quote: In the morning I shaved
issues.justification: Slightly clunky lyric phrasing; 'I shaved at dawn/this morning' might sing better in English.

issues.translation_quote: Clever how they tucked you away.
issues.justification: Comprehensible, but 'tucked you away' is an odd choice for institutional confinement; 'packed you off/locked you away' would fit better.

issues.translation_quote: Well... Today you’re quite the good fellow.
issues.justification: Awkward and overly literal; it doesn't sound like natural spoken praise in English.

issues.translation_quote: I didn’t close my eyes!
issues.justification: Literal rendition of an idiom. 'I didn't sleep a wink' would be more idiomatic.

issues.source_quote: Я похож на какого-то стилягу. На прощелыгу.
issues.translation_quote: I look like some kind of hipster. A swindler.
issues.justification: The pairing is semantically understandable but tonally awkward in English; the comic self-mockery could be sharper.

issues.translation_quote: Total alles kaput.
issues.justification: Retaining the Germanism may be defensible, but without adaptation it can sound random rather than comic bombast to English viewers.

issues.source_quote: Тот караулит, этот спит и так весь мир вертится!
issues.translation_quote: One keeps watch, the other sleeps— and so the whole world turns!
issues.justification: Mostly accurate, but the poetic line remains stiff and doesn’t quite flow as English verse.
